generation.author: aiden-agent
generation.runtime: Agent-owned tools and execution-specific Bash; no required factory action bundle.

dependencyDecision.NO_CHANGE: No new or changed infrastructure requirement; do not select a capability. Existing unchanged dependencies are not a delta.
dependencyDecision.CHANGE_REQUIRED: Exactly one registered, application-eligible capability supported by source evidence.
dependencyDecision.BLOCKED: Unknown or ambiguous requirement, unsupported modification/removal, incomplete evidence, or conflicting baseline. Never treat a failed scan as NO_CHANGE.

terraformRoot.requiredFilesScope: BOOTSTRAP scaffold only; existing roots are classified semantically, not by filename

existingRootPolicy.backend: Preserve the contract-matched app-owned S3 backend, state key and execution identity
existingRootPolicy.generation: Agent-authored scoped extension of the actual existing root; preserve existing declarations, provider selections and externally managed resources
existingRootPolicy.resourceUpdates: Only scoped, reviewed changes supported by the feature request; change authorization is owned by external OPA/platform governance, not a factory action allowlist.
existingRootPolicy.noChange: Resource-free existing roots are supported. Missing lockfile or delivery artifacts require DELIVERY_BOOTSTRAP with zero resource changes

permissionsBoundary.bootstrap: Persist the configured ARN as the generated root variable default, or a literal role argument, so native Harness Plan and Apply use the same value without runner-only environment overrides. Omitted means null, not a chosen policy.
permissionsBoundary.extend: Preserve existing backend, provider configuration, resource ownership and role boundaries while adding necessary capability configuration. A configured boundary must already match the root, state and live role; otherwise block for an operator-reviewed migration.
permissionsBoundary.policyOwnership: Pre-existing platform policy. Do not create, update, delete, or select a replacement policy during delivery.

deliveryPipeline.referenceUse: For a new/reference-based pipeline, copy this pinned YAML and substitute application settings. CI owns checkout, test containers and native BuildAndPushECR; do not reintroduce a delegate ShellScript that creates Kubernetes build Jobs. Preserve compatible existing external pipelines unless a reviewed migration is authorized.
deliveryPipeline.immutableRevision: Build, Terraform configuration, service manifests and deployed artifact must correlate to the same verified deployment_commit_sha; equivalent immutable input bindings are allowed.
deliveryPipeline.compatibility: Verify behavior using full resolved definitions, input sets and templates. Discover actual node paths and input bindings. Identifiers, variable names, extra validation steps and otherwise valid ordering need not match the reference.
deliveryPipeline.ordering: Native Plan precedes native Apply of that same plan. Deployment follows its required build and provisioning. Build may precede Terraform when its repository and other prerequisites already exist.
deliveryPipeline.existingResources: Preserve resource identities. Differences from the reference are not authorization to rewrite a live pipeline. Genuine gaps require a scoped reviewed correction.
deliveryPipeline.monitoring: Persist source/deployment/pipeline/execution identity; resolve and inspect native nodes by verified mapping and type, not template identifiers. Ambiguous trigger outcomes require reconciliation, never blind retry.
deliveryPipeline.enforcement: Platform owners configure external policy enforcement outside this workflow. The agent reports observed policy denials or pending approvals accurately, but neither provisions governance nor claims security certification.
deliveryPipeline.governance: External OPA/platform governance owns change authorization. Do not generate or execute a factory plan-policy script, duplicate its rules, require a factory guard, or audit edit/bypass separation as a delivery prerequisite. Preserve and honor existing policy decisions, approvals, permissions and branch protections; do not weaken or bypass them. A successful plan is not policy approval.

validation.plan: Normal refresh-enabled speculative plan for validity, review and source/state correlation; change approval belongs to external governance.
